faq.question: How much do property managers charge in Jersey City?
faq.answer: Most quotes follow the statewide pattern of 8% to 12% of monthly collected rent plus a leasing fee, with flat monthly fees as the main alternative. On common Jersey City rents of $1,400 to $3,200, a percentage fee runs roughly $112 to $384 a month.

faq.question: Is my building covered by Jersey City rent control?
faq.answer: The City treats buildings with five or more units as covered unless it has an exemption on file, such as the state's 30-year exemption for new construction. Coverage is building-specific — check the City's rent control map, use the rent control lookup tool above as a starting point, and confirm with the City's Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations.

faq.question: Should I pay a percentage or a flat fee in Jersey City?
faq.answer: Compare what each structure covers, not just the monthly number. A percentage of collected rent ties the manager’s pay to rent actually collected: if the unit sits empty or the tenant doesn’t pay, the manager isn’t paid that month. A flat monthly fee is easier to forecast but is generally owed whether or not rent comes in. Either way, ask what sits outside the fee, such as leasing, renewals and maintenance markups. PPM charges 10% of monthly rent collected, never more than $275 per unit (at least $150 in a month the rent is collected in full), plus a $395 fee for each new lease.
